---
name: sites
description: Use Sites when the user wants a website built for them (including a landing page, portfolio, dashboard, portal, tracker, hub, game, event registration, or tool), requests changes to a website already built with Sites, wants to publish a website with Sites, or wants to manage Sites hosting.
---

# Sites

Take the requested website through the supported development and publishing workflow. Publish completed new Sites and edits unless the user requests local-only work or saving without deployment. New Sites start private; preserve an existing Site's audience unless the user requests a change. Native tool approvals apply without an additional conversational publishing gate.

For hosting-only changes, use the relevant native Sites tool and confirm its returned state; source preparation is needed only for source changes or publication.

## Workflow

`<plugin-root>` is the installed directory containing `scripts/` and `skills/`. Run helpers with absolute paths and literal arguments from the selected checkout. Keep credentials in session memory and pass them through stdin, never shell arguments, files, or output.

### 1. Select and open

Default to a new Site unless a specific existing Site is identified.

- **Existing hosted Site:** retain its `project_id` and audience, call `get_site` and `create_source_repository_write_credential`, and open with the [source helper](#source-helper) before editing. Omit `archivePath`; use an empty directory when source is missing, then the returned `checkout_path`.
- **New Site:** create a unique, new empty project subdirectory in the task's workspace, normally `/workspace/sites/<slug>` in managed Linux. Use the supplied Vinext starter by default. If the user requests another framework or implementation, skip the provided Vinext starter and build directly with their choice. For hosting, either path must meet the minimum deploy format under [Hosting manifest](#hosting-manifest). Preserve retained templates.
- **Local-only:** use the available checkout; skip registration, source synchronization, and publication.

### 2. Prepare and launch

For new Vinext projects, run:

```text
node <plugin-root>/scripts/project-setup.mjs
```

This copies the starter and configures ignored checkout-local state. Helpers select `managed-linux` only for `SITES_MANAGED_LINUX_CONTAINER=1`, otherwise `portable`. For buildless HTML/JS, prepare `dist/` for `index.html` and assets; skip starter setup, installation, and build.

For a retained template, add `--template-source <absolute-sanitized-source-directory>`; exclude Site identity, Git metadata, credentials, and runtime data. For explicitly requested Worker ESM, add `--starter worker-esm` and follow [its README](templates/worker-esm-starter/README.md). Use [Troubleshooting](references/troubleshooting.md#project-configuration) for profile repair or static-to-Worker migration.

After minimal setup, launch registration for new hosted work in a retained execution cell when available. Native `create_site` creates a private, unpublished Site and returns its ID and source credential. Immediately persist the ID when it returns. For static Sites, include `--static-directory` when known to set both fields at once; omit it for Worker builds. For buildless HTML/JS, run:

```text
node <plugin-root>/scripts/set-project-id.mjs --project-id <returned-id> --static-directory dist
```

Reuse an existing ID or registration attempt; resolve uncertain creation before retrying. For app integrations, first read [discovery and declarations](references/app-integrations.md#discover-and-declare).

Start needed dependency installation before feature implementation:

```text
node <plugin-root>/scripts/install-dependencies.mjs
```

Run only when dependencies are missing or their inputs changed. The installer handles host settings, package-manager selection, and interrupted setup; it takes no flags. Use one installer; keep dependency inputs unchanged while it runs. Proceed to implementation once the applicable operations are launched.

For managed-image pnpm additions, use `node "$SITES_PNPM_BIN" add <package>`.

Start required image search or generation when its brief is clear, alongside independent source work. Consider a parallel subagent for image downloads. Delegate bounded asset or research tasks; the Site owner handles the checkout, native Sites calls in the owning conversation, and publication.

### 3. Implement

Write application files while setup runs. For hosted work, await persisted Site identity before further manifest edits or source synchronization. Await installed dependencies before commands that need them.

Implement the requested experience in one focused pass; revise for observed failures or unmet requirements. Replace starter title and description and remove temporary `codex-preview` metadata during implementation. Integrate required assets and complete the requested behavior before publishing.

When `SITES_MANAGED_LINUX_CONTAINER=1`, preview is internal QA. Start it only when the task needs browser QA and `cua_repl.js` is available. If `cua_repl.js` is unavailable, skip browser QA: do not start a preview server, install a browser, or improvise another browser-control path.

When `SITES_MANAGED_LINUX_CONTAINER` is not `1`, use local preview. In visible tasks with user-facing preview support, show the first recognizable version once it serves successfully and keep it current. Background tasks skip user-facing handoff.

Before any preview, browser test, or screenshot, read the selected reference: [managed](references/preview/managed.md) or [local](references/preview/local.md). If preview infrastructure is unavailable, report the verification limit and continue appropriate checks and publication unless passing browser QA is required. Follow [Troubleshooting](references/troubleshooting.md#preview) after failures.

### 4. Validate and package

Collect any remaining registration and installation results, then finalize the source manifest before checks/builds and packaging.

#### Hosting manifest

The tracked `.openai/hosting.json` declares Site identity and deployment configuration. After registration, a minimal static Site uses:

```json
{
  "project_id": "<returned-id>",
  "static": {"directory": "dist"}
}
```

| Field | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `project_id` | Persist with `set-project-id.mjs` on creation; preserve on updates. |
| `static` | Object with `directory`: `dist`, `dist/client`, `out`, `build`, or `.output/public`. Omit for Worker builds. |
| `d1`, `r2` | [Storage bindings](references/storage.md#bindings); leave unused bindings `null`. |
| `capabilities` | Declare [a Site MCP server](references/site-mcp-server.md#build-the-server) when needed. |
| `plugins`, `connectors` | [App integration declarations](references/app-integrations.md#discover-and-declare). |

A deployable Site needs `.openai/hosting.json` with its `project_id` and one of these build outputs:

- **Static:** Set `static.directory` to a supported directory listed above. It must contain `index.html` and the assets the page uses.
- **Server-backed:** Omit `static`. Build a Cloudflare Worker ES module at `dist/server/index.js` that default-exports an object with a `fetch` handler.

Preserve existing fields. Edit the source manifest; build helpers emit Worker deployment metadata.

Run checks appropriate to the change; lint only when requested. For hosted work, package with the source helper using remaining checks/builds as ordered argument arrays and an absolute `archivePath`. Pass the complete prior opening result as `source` when available.

Buildless HTML/JS uses `commands: []` when no checks remain. Framework projects, including Vinext and static exports, build with `["node", "<plugin-root>/scripts/build-site.mjs"]`. Omit commands already completed successfully with unchanged inputs. Local-only work runs checks/builds directly and skips packaging for publication.

#### Source helper

Use the repository access from registration or `create_source_repository_write_credential` for the same Site. If `auth_mode` is `work_proxy`, it contains no token. Use the same helper or ordinary Git with `remote_url`; Work supplies authentication outside the executor. If Git reports expired access, call `create_source_repository_write_credential` again. Do not configure a token or authentication header for this mode.

```text
node <plugin-root>/scripts/site-workflow.mjs --project-id <project_id>
```

Launch with `exec_command(tty: true, yield_time_ms: 1000)`. After `Ready for Site workflow JSON on stdin (input is hidden).`, send one newline-terminated JSON object with `write_stdin`. Wait for successful exit and retain the final JSON result.

| Input | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `credential` | Returned credential object, through stdin only. |
| `source` | Complete prior opening result, when available. |
| `commands` | Remaining checks/builds as ordered argument arrays; packaging only. |
| `archivePath` | Absolute output archive path for packaging; omit for opening. |

The helper owns Git preparation, ordered commands, commit/push, and packaging. Pass its verified `project_id`, `commit_sha`, and `archive` directly to publishing; keep the archive unchanged until saving succeeds.

### 5. Publish

Use the audience from creation or `get_site`; refresh unknown or changed ownership/access before selecting a tool.

| Audience | Native calls |
| --- | --- |
| Confirmed owner-private | `save_version_and_deploy_private`; if unavailable, `save_site_version` then `deploy_private_site_version`. |
| Other supported audiences | `save_site_version` then `deploy_site_version`. |

Save-only uses `save_site_version` without deployment. A matching archive-backed saved version needs only deployment; source-only versions still need their matching archive. Preserve returned version IDs, including `saved_version_id`, when resuming. Continue an existing deployment rather than starting another.

### 6. Finish

Poll `get_deployment_status` only for `pending`, `building`, or `publishing`; stop on a terminal result. A successful native result with its URL verifies deployment without another status call or browser visit.

Return the literal deployed URL, saved version for save-only work, or local result. In visible tasks, open the deployed URL in the existing Site tab with `open_in_codex` or equivalent when supported; background tasks skip browser handoff. Handoff failure does not invalidate a verified deployment. Report incomplete verification or blockers; read [Troubleshooting](references/troubleshooting.md) after a failure or incomplete result.

## Design

Build around the user's primary task. Choose a coherent visual direction suited to the subject and audience, and preserve established branding when editing. Keep layouts responsive, text readable, and interactions accessible. Use imagery when it contributes to the experience.

Keep functionality within the requested scope. For open-ended presentation-led briefs, develop content and structure as needed for a complete experience. Preserve explicit content constraints and keep bounded edits bounded.

Read applicable guidance before choosing content and structure. Select by the experience's purpose, not merely its visual subject.

| Design guidance | When to use it |
| --- | --- |
| [Presentation-led sites](references/design/presentation-led.md) | New websites primarily meant to introduce, explain, persuade, or showcase: landing pages, marketing sites, portfolios, and interactive presentation sites. |

## Capabilities

Choose capabilities from the requested behavior and preserve those an existing Site uses. This is a reference index, not a checklist of features to add. Read only the relevant pages.

| Capability | When to use it |
| --- | --- |
| [Data and files](references/storage.md) | Durable records in D1 and uploads or generated files in R2. |
| [Identity and access](references/identity-and-secrets.md) | ChatGPT sign-in, user-owned data, runtime secrets, and private service access. |
| [App integrations](references/app-integrations.md) | Let the Site read data and perform actions in apps visitors have connected to ChatGPT. |
| [Site MCP server](references/site-mcp-server.md) | Expose the Site's operations as tools agents can call. |
| [Browser agent support (WebMCP)](references/browser-agent-support.md) | Optionally make the page's actions easier for browser agents to use. |
| [Scheduled updates](references/recurring-updates.md) | Update a published Site while it is closed, using an unattended data path and a linked automation. |

Hosted server code runs in Cloudflare Workers, with 128 MB per isolate and HTTP-based external connections; raw TCP is unavailable. When using the Vinext starter, preserve its `sites()` build integration. Capability references specify any required manifest declarations; not every feature is a `capabilities` entry.

"""Durable IT access request intake."""

from .app import Intake

__all__ = ["Intake"]
"""Run with python -m intake; offline operation needs no installation."""

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

from .app import Intake
from .extraction import ROOT


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Durable IT access-request intake")
    subs = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    benchmark = subs.add_parser("benchmark", help="isolated mocked workload verification; never calls a provider")
    benchmark.add_argument("--sizes", type=int, nargs="+", default=[200, 400, 2000])
    benchmark.add_argument("--scenarios", nargs="+", choices=["normal", "slow", "throttled", "concurrent", "interrupted"],
                           default=["normal", "slow", "throttled", "concurrent", "interrupted"])
    benchmark.add_argument("--report", default="benchmarks/results.json")
    benchmark.add_argument("--storage-dir", help="local parent for isolated temporary benchmark data")
    benchmark.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=4)
    benchmark.add_argument("--latency-seconds", type=float, default=.005)
    benchmark.add_argument("--poll-seconds", type=float, default=.1)
    benchmark.add_argument("--timeout-seconds", type=float, default=600)
    benchmark.add_argument("--publication-interval-seconds", type=float)
    benchmark.add_argument("--lease-seconds", type=float, default=30)
    for name in ("intake", "resume", "retry", "refresh-policy", "queue", "status", "export", "verify", "migrate", "accuracy", "evidence"):
        sub = subs.add_parser(name)
        sub.add_argument("--source", default="materials/requests")
        sub.add_argument("--output", default="deliverables")
        sub.add_argument("--state", help="SQLite path on local durable storage")
        sub.add_argument("--policy", help="policy text to version with the deployed routing implementation")
        if name in ("intake", "resume", "retry", "accuracy", "evidence"):
            sub.add_argument("--mock", action="store_true", help="replay labeled fixtures; no model call")
        if name in ("intake", "retry"):
            sub.add_argument("--documents", nargs="+", help="export filenames")
        if name in ("intake", "resume", "retry"):
            sub.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=4)
        if name == "intake":
            sub.add_argument("--force", action="store_true")
            sub.add_argument("--submit-only", action="store_true", help="register work and return a resumable batch ID")
        if name == "resume":
            sub.add_argument("batch_id")
            sub.add_argument("--saved-config", action="store_true", help="restore the batch's saved settings")
        if name == "retry":
            sub.add_argument("--current-config", action="store_true", help="intentionally replace saved settings with the current environment")
        if name == "status":
            sub.add_argument("--batch")
        if name == "accuracy":
            sub.add_argument("--expectations", help="source-derived expectation manifest")
            sub.add_argument("--purpose-reviews", help="source-grounded purpose adjudications bound to source/extraction hashes")
            sub.add_argument("--fail-on-errors", action="store_true", help="exit nonzero when any factual/evidence/review quality check fails")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.command == "benchmark":
        from .benchmark import run_benchmarks
        result = run_benchmarks(args.sizes, args.scenarios, args.report, args.storage_dir, args.workers,
                                args.latency_seconds, poll_seconds=args.poll_seconds,
                                timeout_seconds=args.timeout_seconds,
                                publication_interval_seconds=args.publication_interval_seconds,
                                lease_seconds=args.lease_seconds)
        print(json.dumps({"report": args.report, "cases": len(result["cases"])}))
        return 0
    mock = getattr(args, "mock", False)
    config = {"provider": "mock", "model": "fixtures-v1"} if mock else None
    app = Intake(args.source, args.output, args.state, config=config, policy_path=args.policy)
    if args.command == "resume" and args.saved_config:
        app = app.for_batch(args.batch_id)
        if args.mock and app.extractor.config["provider"] != "mock":
            parser.error("--mock cannot replay saved provider settings; submit a new mock intake")
        mock = app.extractor.config["provider"] == "mock"
    responder = None
    if mock:
        from .fixtures import fixture_response
        responder = fixture_response

    kwargs = {"responder": responder, "response_source": "mock" if mock else None}
    if args.command == "intake":
        docs = args.documents
        if docs and any(Path(d).name != d for d in docs):
            parser.error("documents must be filenames")
        if docs is None and not app.source.is_dir():
            parser.error("source directory does not exist or is not a directory")
        paths = [app.source / d for d in docs] if docs else None
        batch = app.submit(paths, force=args.force)
        # Flushed before any network work: usable after interruption.
        print(json.dumps({"batch_id": batch}), flush=True)
        result = {"batch_id": batch} if args.submit_only else app.resume(batch, workers=args.workers, **kwargs)
    elif args.command == "resume":
        result = app.resume(args.batch_id, workers=args.workers, **kwargs)
    elif args.command == "retry":
        result = app.retry_failed(args.documents, current_config=args.current_config, workers=args.workers, **kwargs)
    elif args.command == "refresh-policy":
        result = app.refresh_policy()
    elif args.command == "status":
        result = {"batches": app.store.batches(), "progress": app.status(args.batch)}
    elif args.command == "queue":
        result = app.queue()
    elif args.command == "export":
        result = app.publish()
    elif args.command == "verify":
        result = app.verify()
        records, queue = app.snapshot()
        submitted = [json.loads(line) for line in (app.output / "extractions.jsonl").read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()]
        submitted_queue = json.loads((app.output / "queue.json").read_text())
        if submitted != records or submitted_queue != queue:
            raise ValueError("verification failed: submission files differ from published snapshot; run export")
    elif args.command == "migrate":
        result = app.import_legacy()
    elif args.command == "accuracy":
        from .accuracy import run_accuracy
        options = {"purpose_reviews_path": args.purpose_reviews}
        if args.expectations:
            options["expectations_path"] = args.expectations
        result = run_accuracy(app, **kwargs, **options)
    else:
        from .reports import write_evidence
        result = write_evidence(app, **kwargs)
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    if isinstance(result, dict) and result.get("failed"):
        return 1
    if isinstance(result, dict) and result.get("error"):
        return 1
    if args.command == "accuracy" and args.fail_on_errors and not result["passed"]:
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

### 3. Implement

Write application files while setup runs. For hosted work, await persisted Site identity before further manifest edits or source synchronization. Await installed dependencies before commands that need them.

Implement the requested experience in one focused pass; revise for observed failures or unmet requirements. Replace starter title and description and remove temporary `codex-preview` metadata during implementation. Integrate required assets and complete the requested behavior before publishing.

When `SITES_MANAGED_LINUX_CONTAINER=1`, preview is internal QA. Start it only when the task needs browser QA and `cua_repl.js` is available. If `cua_repl.js` is unavailable, skip browser QA: do not start a preview server, install a browser, or improvise another browser-control path.

When `SITES_MANAGED_LINUX_CONTAINER` is not `1`, use local preview. In visible tasks with user-facing preview support, show the first recognizable version once it serves successfully and keep it current. Background tasks skip user-facing handoff.

Before any preview, browser test, or screenshot, read the selected reference: [managed](references/preview/managed.md) or [local](references/preview/local.md). If preview infrastructure is unavailable, report the verification limit and continue appropriate checks and publication unless passing browser QA is required. Collect any remaining registration and installation results, then finalize the source manifest before checks/builds and packaging.

#### Hosting manifest

The tracked `.openai/hosting.json` declares Site identity and deployment configuration. After registration, a minimal static Site uses:

```json
{
  "project_id": "<returned-id>",
  "static": {"directory": "dist"}
}
```

| Field | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `project_id` | Persist with `set-project-id.mjs` on creation; preserve on updates. |
| `static` | Object with `directory`: `dist`, `dist/client`, `out`, `build`, or `.output/public`. Omit for Worker builds. |
| `d1`, `r2` | [Storage bindings](references/storage.md#bindings); leave unused bindings `null`. |
| `capabilities` | Declare [a Site MCP server](references/site-mcp-server.md#build-the-server) when needed. |
| `plugins`, `connectors` | [App integration declarations](references/app-integrations.md#discover-and-declare). |

A deployable Site needs `.openai/hosting.json` with its `project_id` and one of these build outputs:

- **Static:** Set `static.directory` to a supported directory listed above. It must contain `index.html` and the assets the page uses.
- **Server-backed:** Omit `static`. Build a Cloudflare Worker ES module at `dist/server/index.js` that default-exports an object with a `fetch` handler.

Preserve existing fields. Edit the source manifest; build helpers emit Worker deployment metadata.

Run checks appropriate to the change; lint only when requested. For hosted work, package with the source helper using remaining checks/builds as ordered argument arrays and an absolute `archivePath`. Pass the complete prior opening result as `source` when available.

Buildless HTML/JS uses `commands: []` when no checks remain. Framework projects, including Vinext and static exports, build with `["node", "<plugin-root>/scripts/build-site.mjs"]`. Omit commands already completed successfully with unchanged inputs. Local-only work runs checks/builds directly and skips packaging for publication.

#### Source helper

Use the repository access from registration or `create_source_repository_write_credential` for the same Site. If `auth_mode` is `work_proxy`, it contains no token. Use the same helper or ordinary Git with `remote_url`; Work supplies authentication outside the executor. If Git reports expired access, call `create_source_repository_write_credential` again. Do not configure a token or authentication header for this mode.

```text
node <plugin-root>/scripts/site-workflow.mjs --project-id <project_id>
```

Launch with `exec_command(tty: true, yield_time_ms: 1000)`. After `Ready for Site workflow JSON on stdin (input is hidden).`, send one newline-terminated JSON object with `write_stdin`. Wait for successful exit and retain the final JSON result.

| Input | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `credential` | Returned credential object, through stdin only. |
| `source` | Complete prior opening result, when available. |
| `commands` | Remaining checks/builds as ordered argument arrays; packaging only. |
| `archivePath` | Absolute output archive path for packaging; omit for opening. |

The helper owns Git preparation, ordered commands, commit/push, and packaging. Pass its verified `project_id`, `commit_sha`, and `archive` directly to publishing; keep the archive unchanged until saving succeeds.

Use the audience from creation or `get_site`; refresh unknown or changed ownership/access before selecting a tool.

| Audience | Native calls |
| --- | --- |
| Confirmed owner-private | `save_version_and_deploy_private`; if unavailable, `save_site_version` then `deploy_private_site_version`. |
| Other supported audiences | `save_site_version` then `deploy_site_version`. |

Save-only uses `save_site_version` without deployment. A matching archive-backed saved version needs only deployment; source-only versions still need their matching archive. Preserve returned version IDs, including `saved_version_id`, when resuming. Continue an existing deployment rather than starting another.

### 6. Finish

Poll `get_deployment_status` only for `pending`, `building`, or `publishing`; stop on a terminal result. A successful native result with its URL verifies deployment without another status call or browser visit.

Return the literal deployed URL, saved version for save-only work, or local result. In visible tasks, open the deployed URL in the existing Site tab with `open_in_codex` or equivalent when supported; background tasks skip browser handoff. Handoff failure does not invalidate a verified deployment. Report incomplete verification or blockers; read [Troubleshooting](references/troubleshooting.md) after a failure or incomplete result.

## Design

Build around the user's primary task. Choose a coherent visual direction suited to the subject and audience, and preserve established branding when editing. Keep layouts responsive, text readable, and interactions accessible. Use imagery when it contributes to the experience.

Keep functionality within the requested scope. For open-ended presentation-led briefs, develop content and structure as needed for a complete experience. Preserve explicit content constraints and keep bounded edits bounded.

Read applicable guidance before choosing content and structure. Select by the experience's purpose, not merely its visual subject.

| Design guidance | When to use it |
| --- | --- |
| [Presentation-led sites](references/design/presentation-led.md) | New websites primarily meant to introduce, explain, persuade, or showcase: landing pages, marketing sites, portfolios, and interactive presentation sites. |

## Capabilities

Choose capabilities from the requested behavior and preserve those an existing Site uses. This is a reference index, not a checklist of features to add. Read only the relevant pages.

| Capability | When to use it |
| --- | --- |
| [Data and files](references/storage.md) | Durable records in D1 and uploads or generated files in R2. |
| [Identity and access](references/identity-and-secrets.md) | ChatGPT sign-in, user-owned data, runtime secrets, and private service access. |
| [App integrations](references/app-integrations.md) | Let the Site read data and perform actions in apps visitors have connected to ChatGPT. |
| [Site MCP server](references/site-mcp-server.md) | Expose the Site's operations as tools agents can call. |
| [Browser agent support (WebMCP)](references/browser-agent-support.md) | Optionally make the page's actions easier for browser agents to use. |
| [Scheduled updates](references/recurring-updates.md) | Update a published Site while it is closed, using an unattended data path and a linked automation. |

"""Browser entry point: flask --app app run (mock responses by default)."""

import os

from intake import Intake
from intake.web import create_app as create_dashboard


def create_app():
    mode = os.getenv("INTAKE_WEB_MODE", "mock")
    if mode not in ("mock", "provider"):
        raise ValueError("INTAKE_WEB_MODE must be mock or provider")
    config = {"provider": "mock", "model": "fixtures-v1"} if mode == "mock" else None
    intake = Intake(source=os.getenv("INTAKE_SOURCE", "materials/requests"),
                    output=os.getenv("INTAKE_OUTPUT", "deliverables"), config=config)
    return create_dashboard(intake, workers=int(os.getenv("INTAKE_WORKERS", "4")))

"""Browser routes and background intake use isolated mock state."""

import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import tempfile
import threading
import unittest
from unittest.mock import patch

from intake import Intake
from intake.extraction import ROOT
from intake.web import create_app
from test_intake import CONFIG, answer, wait_for


@unittest.skipUnless(importlib.util.find_spec("flask"), "Install requirements-web.lock for browser tests")
class WebTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.base = Path(self.temp.name)
        self.source = self.base / "requests"
        self.source.mkdir()
        for doc in ("IT-001.json", "IT-002.json"):
            shutil.copy(ROOT / "materials/requests" / doc, self.source)
        self.intake = Intake(self.source, self.base / "output", config=CONFIG)
        self.web = create_app(self.intake)
        self.web.config["TESTING"] = True
        self.client = self.web.test_client()
        self.dashboard = self.web.extensions["intake_dashboard"]

    def tearDown(self):
        wait_for(lambda: not self.dashboard.running)
        self.temp.cleanup()

    def test_page_assets_and_no_filesystem_exposure(self):
        page = self.client.get("/")
        self.assertEqual(page.status_code, 200)
        self.assertIn(b"Review queue", page.data)
        for path, content_type in (("/assets/app.js", "javascript"), ("/assets/style.css", "text/css")):
            result = self.client.get(path)
            self.assertEqual(result.status_code, 200)
            self.assertIn(content_type, result.content_type)
        for path in ("/materials/requests/IT-001.json", "/.git/config", "/assets/../../app.py"):
            self.assertEqual(self.client.get(path).status_code, 404)

    def test_state_contains_queue_facts_without_private_configuration(self):
        self.intake.run(responder=answer, response_source="mock")
        response = self.client.get("/api/state")
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        state = response.json
        self.assertTrue(state["mock"])
        self.assertEqual(len(state["requests"]), 2)
        record = state["requests"][0]
        self.assertEqual(record["extraction"]["requester"], "Maya Chen")
        self.assertTrue(record["extraction"]["supporting_quotes"])
        self.assertNotIn("processing_config", record)
        self.assertNotIn("base_url", response.get_data(as_text=True))

    def test_mock_intake_runs_asynchronously_and_reuses_unchanged_results(self):
        first = self.client.post("/api/intake", json={})
        self.assertEqual(first.status_code, 202)
        self.assertTrue(first.json["batch_id"])
        wait_for(lambda: not self.dashboard.running)
        self.assertEqual(self.client.get("/api/state").json["progress"]["counts"]["completed"], 2)
        with patch.object(self.intake.extractor, "extract", side_effect=AssertionError("unexpected extraction")):
            self.assertEqual(self.client.post("/api/intake", json={}).status_code, 202)
            wait_for(lambda: not self.dashboard.running)
        state = self.client.get("/api/state").json
        self.assertIsNone(state["task_error"])
        self.assertEqual(state["progress"]["counts"]["reused"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(len(state["requests"]), 2)

        entered, release = threading.Event(), threading.Event()
        original = self.intake.resume

            release.wait(5)
            return original(*args, **kwargs)

            try:
                self.assertEqual(self.client.post("/api/intake", json={}).status_code, 202)
                self.assertTrue(entered.wait(3))

                self.assertEqual(self.client.post("/api/intake", json={}).status_code, 409)
            finally:
                release.set()
                wait_for(lambda: not self.dashboard.running)

        self.assertEqual(self.client.get("/api/state", base_url="http://untrusted.invalid").status_code, 400)
        self.assertEqual(self.intake.store.batches(), [])

    def test_errors_are_visible_without_returning_raw_exceptions(self):
        with patch.object(self.intake, "resume", side_effect=ValueError("private-token-value")):
            self.assertEqual(self.client.post("/api/intake", json={}).status_code, 202)
            wait_for(lambda: not self.dashboard.running)
        response = self.client.get("/api/state")
        self.assertIn("interrupted", response.json["task_error"])

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 503)
        self.assertNotIn("private-token-value", response.get_data(as_text=True))

        self.assertTrue(imported.verify().startswith("PASS"))

section='''## Browser dashboard (Flask)

Install the optional browser dependencies and start the app from the repository
root:

```bash
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements-web.lock
flask --app app run
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:5000**. The dashboard displays the existing review queue,
supports search and owner/status filters, and shows each request's extracted
facts, exact evidence quotes, review notes and next action. **Run mock intake**
starts work in the background; completed results update automatically. There are
no access-approval controls. Stop the local server with Ctrl+C. If running on a
remote development host, forward port 5000 to your computer before opening it.

The Flask entry point uses mock responses by default, with no API key needed.
It shares the CLI's durable state. On a fresh checkout, existing committed outputs
are imported without provider calls. An empty output directory starts with an
empty queue until intake is run. `INTAKE_SOURCE`, `INTAKE_OUTPUT`, `INTAKE_STATE`
and `INTAKE_WORKERS` configure its paths and workers. To deliberately use the
configured live provider instead, set `INTAKE_WEB_MODE=provider` along with the
provider environment variables below before starting Flask.

An equivalent command using the existing CLI is:

```bash
python -m intake serve --mock --port 5000
```

Flask and its transitive dependencies are pinned in `requirements-web.lock` and
declared as the optional `web` dependency group in `pyproject.toml`. The core CLI
remains usable without Flask. Run the full suite including browser route tests
inside the virtual environment:

```bash
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Without the web dependencies, browser tests are explicitly skipped. Browser tests
exercise Flask routes, mock intake/reuse, concurrent reads, duplicate start
protection, request validation, redacted errors and fresh-checkout import.

'''

assert needle in s
s=s.replace(needle,section+needle,1)
s=s.replace('database adapter, HTTP server, shared automatic rate limiter or history cleanup', 'database adapter, shared automatic rate limiter or history cleanup')
p.write_text(s)

# AI Full Stack Challenge — IT Access Requests

## The task
Northstar Labs receives access requests as free-text messages. Build a small runnable application that uses a language model to turn those messages into structured records and a review queue for the IT team. The supplied company, people and requests are fictional.

Read docs/requirements.md for the operating context and required behavior, materials/office-policy.md for review rules, and snapshot.schema.json for the record format. The 20 JSON exports in materials/requests/ are your starting data. Choose an interface suited to the IT team: a CLI, service or web application. Operators should be able to start intake, inspect completed results while other requests are pending, and resume unfinished work through the documented interface.

## What to submit
This brief ships as CHALLENGE.md; the README.md below is yours to write.

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| README.md | Setup, supported runtime/provider, exact intake/test/accuracy-check commands, environment-variable names, and how to inspect the queue |
| Source code and dependency lockfile | Runnable application, extraction prompt, schema and model request configuration |
| deliverables/extractions.jsonl | One current record per message: document_id, source_sha256, extraction (schema-conforming object, or null on error), status, owner, next_action, error (null on success), and response_source (`mock`, or the provider and model ID that produced the record) |
| deliverables/queue.json | The review queue linked to extraction records by document_id |
| deliverables/accuracy.md | Source-derived expected fields for the 20 supplied messages and one paraphrase you author; the field-comparison procedure, exact-match counting/denominator rules, factual-error reporting and model/configuration; distinguish mocked examples from any optional live observations |
| deliverables/request-evidence.json | Credential-redacted example model request showing the model ID and configuration used, plus the implemented response handling |
| deliverables/verification.md | Verification commands and assertions, their intended comparisons, operating limits, and any observed results or repairs clearly identified as such |
| Coding-session capture | Session record paired with the submitted commit, collected through the facilitator's capture setup |

## Submission
Commit and push the application, outputs and session capture to your repository's default branch. Submit only the root repository link (`https://github.com/<your-account>/<repository>`) through the Classroom assignment. The facilitator supplies the assignment and capture instructions.

Submit the implemented provider integration and source-grounded validation procedure. Use mocked responses for reproducible development examples, and label each recorded observation with its configuration and whether it used a mock or provider response. The committed deliverables may come from mocked or provider responses; each record's response_source says which.
# AI Full Stack Challenge — IT Access Requests

Northstar Labs access-request intake uses a language model to extract source facts,
validates them against `snapshot.schema.json`, and applies `materials/office-policy.md`
to prepare a queue for human review. It never approves access.

The application is the `intake/` Python package. The browser dashboard, CLI and
`AI Full Stack Access Request Intake.ipynb` notebook use the same implementation.
Each completed document is saved immediately, even while other requests are pending.

The current submission outputs were regenerated offline on 2026-11-10 and are
explicitly labeled `response_source: mock`. Original 2026-11-06 provider outputs
and reports are preserved in `deliverables/historical/2026-11-06/`, with SHA-256
checksums. See `deliverables/verification.md` for current component checks and
known accuracy limitations; mock replay does not establish provider accuracy.

## Runtime and setup

Use CPython 3.10–3.12 on a single Linux application host with a **local persistent
disk**. Tested here with Python 3.12.3. The core CLI and its tests use the standard library;
`requirements.lock` records the empty third-party dependency set. Run commands
from the repository root; no package installation is required.

```bash
python --version
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python -m intake intake --mock --output /tmp/northstar-demo
python -m intake queue --output /tmp/northstar-demo
python -m intake verify --output /tmp/northstar-demo
```

Mock mode replays `tests/fixtures/responses.json`, derived from the earlier
committed extraction outputs. These are development fixtures, **not independently
authored accuracy expectations**. Records are labeled `response_source: mock`.
Mock and provider configurations have different fingerprints, preventing mock
results from being reused as live results. Unknown documents need new mock
fixtures or live extraction.

Multiple operator processes may use the same local state database and output
directory on that host. SQLite over NFS, Databricks Workspace/Volumes, or between
separate serverless/cluster hosts is unsupported. A multi-host deployment needs a
shared transactional database adapter; this version does not implement one.
Keep the database, source exports and history on persistent storage and back them
up. `/tmp` in these examples is for disposable demonstrations only.

## Browser dashboard (Flask)

Install the optional browser dependencies and start the app from the repository
root:

```bash
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements-web.lock
flask --app app run
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:5000**. The dashboard displays the existing review queue,
supports search and owner/status filters, and shows each request's extracted
facts, exact evidence quotes, review notes and next action. **Run mock intake**
starts work in the background; completed results update automatically. There are
no access-approval controls. Stop the local server with Ctrl+C. If running on a
remote development host, forward port 5000 to your computer before opening it.

The Flask entry point uses mock responses by default, with no API key needed.
It shares the CLI's durable state. On a fresh checkout, existing committed outputs
are imported without provider calls. An empty output directory starts with an
empty queue until intake is run. `INTAKE_SOURCE`, `INTAKE_OUTPUT`, `INTAKE_STATE`
and `INTAKE_WORKERS` configure its paths and workers. To deliberately use the
configured live provider instead, set `INTAKE_WEB_MODE=provider` along with the
provider environment variables below before starting Flask.

An equivalent command using the existing CLI is:

```bash
python -m intake serve --mock --port 5000
```

Flask and its transitive dependencies are pinned in `requirements-web.lock` and
declared as the optional `web` dependency group in `pyproject.toml`. The core CLI
remains usable without Flask. Run the full suite including browser route tests
inside the virtual environment:

```bash
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Without the web dependencies, browser tests are explicitly skipped. Browser tests
exercise Flask routes, mock intake/reuse, concurrent reads, duplicate start
protection, request validation, redacted errors and fresh-checkout import.

## Live provider configuration

The implemented provider is Databricks AI Gateway Chat Completions:
`POST <workspace-url>/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1/chat/completions`, with strict JSON schema
response formatting and default model `system.ai.gpt-6-luna`. The original
2026-11-06 outputs document observations of that configuration; the refactored
client has been tested offline, not against the live provider in this session.
Availability and permissions depend on your workspace.

For API-key authentication, supply these through your environment or secret
manager:

```bash
export INTAKE_AUTH=api_key
export INTAKE_BASE_URL=https://your-workspace-host
# Supply API_KEY through your environment; never commit it.
python -m intake intake
```

For notebook workspace authentication, use `INTAKE_AUTH=workspace`; the Databricks
SDK is imported lazily only when making a live call. This optional path depends
on the SDK already provided by your notebook runtime. It is not needed by offline
commands or API-key authentication. The notebook must run on the same supported
application host/storage arrangement as the CLI. The old assumption that separate
Databricks serverless resources could safely share filesystem state is superseded.

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `API_KEY` | unset | Live bearer credential; never stored in state or evidence |
| `INTAKE_AUTH` | `api_key` if API_KEY exists, otherwise `workspace` | Authentication strategy |
| `INTAKE_BASE_URL` | unset | Workspace origin; required with API-key auth, otherwise SDK host |
| `INTAKE_API_PATH` | `mlflow/v1/chat/completions` | Relative Chat Completions endpoint beneath `/ai-gateway/` |
| `INTAKE_MODEL` | `system.ai.gpt-6-luna` | Model service identifier |
| `INTAKE_MAX_TOKENS` | `4000` | Completion token limit |
| `INTAKE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `90` | HTTP timeout |
| `INTAKE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `4` | Retryable extraction attempts |
| `INTAKE_WORKERS` | `4` | Python API/notebook worker count; CLI `--workers` defaults to 4 |
| `INTAKE_LEASE_SECONDS` | `30` | Worker claim duration; heartbeat every third of this interval |
| `INTAKE_PUBLISH_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | `1` | Shared-state publication cadence; `0` requests publication after each completion |
| `INTAKE_STATE` | `<output>/.state/intake.sqlite3` | Local durable SQLite path; CLI `--state` overrides it |
| `INTAKE_SOURCE` | `materials/requests` | Notebook source path; CLI uses `--source` |
| `INTAKE_OUTPUT` | `deliverables` | Notebook output path; CLI uses `--output` |
| `INTAKE_POLICY_PATH` | `materials/office-policy.md` in this repository | Policy text to version with deployed routing code; CLI `--policy` overrides it |

The settings fingerprint includes provider, model, normalized effective endpoint
origin and API path, token limit, prompt/version, schema and extraction/validation
implementation. Workspace hosts are resolved before reuse decisions. Credentials
and operational retry/worker settings are excluded. Each job and result stores a
credential-free `processing_config`, including its actual timeout/retry settings.
Temperature is omitted, preserving provider defaults.

Policy versions combine policy text and routing implementation hashes. Routing
code changes do not invalidate extraction fingerprints. Restart operator processes
after deploying code changes, then refresh policy. Old pending batches whose
extraction implementation changed require a new intake; completed results stay
in history. Policy text is versioned evidence: changing business rules also needs
the corresponding deterministic routing implementation, rather than interpreting
arbitrary policy prose automatically.

## Intake, progress and recovery

```bash
# Process new, changed and failed documents; reuse compatible successful results.
python -m intake intake

# Process selected exports. Absence from a batch never withdraws older requests.
python -m intake intake --documents IT-001.json IT-007.json

# Register work without starting model calls. Prints a durable batch_id.
python -m intake intake --submit-only

# The intake command also prints its batch_id before extraction starts.
python -m intake status
python -m intake status --batch BATCH_ID
python -m intake resume BATCH_ID

# Restore the batch's saved model/endpoint/timeout/retry configuration.
python -m intake resume BATCH_ID --saved-config

# Retry current failures, or force a named document to be extracted again.
python -m intake retry
python -m intake retry --documents IT-003.json

# Intentionally use current settings instead of the saved configuration.
python -m intake retry --documents IT-003.json --current-config

# Reroute every current record under deployed policy without model calls.
python -m intake refresh-policy

# Force all supplied documents to be extracted again.
python -m intake intake --force
```

All commands accept `--source`, `--output`, `--state` and `--policy`. Use `--mock`
for new mock intake. Saved-configuration resume and retries automatically replay
saved mock configurations. `--mock` cannot silently override a saved provider
configuration; select `--current-config --mock` to change it deliberately.

Default resume requires compatible settings; `--saved-config` restores them from
the batch. Retries restore each document's saved model, endpoint, auth strategy,
timeout and retry limits, even if the current environment changed. Mixed-settings
retries create separate batches. Credentials still come from the environment or
workspace runtime and must be valid for the saved endpoint. Each failed queue item
includes its exact retry command and paths. Legacy records without saved settings,
or records from a different extraction implementation, need an explicit
`--current-config` choice (legacy queue commands include that flag).

Unreadable exports are independent error records with `source_read_error`, zero
model attempts and `source_sha256: null`: bytes that could not be read cannot have
a source hash. The earlier successful result remains in history. Invalid JSON or
non-string messages keep the hash of their captured bytes and fail without a model
call. Restore the source and use its retry command. `verify` checks the recorded
unreadable-source failure; retry is what processes newly available bytes.

Response handling distinguishes timeouts and connection failures, records structured
error details and an attempt log, and retries 429/5xx, malformed responses/output
and schema failures with exponential backoff and jitter. When supplied, Retry-After
delta-seconds or HTTP-date is a minimum wait; a long value keeps that document
running with a renewed lease. Other documents continue. Authentication errors,
refusals/content filtering and length truncation are terminal for that extraction.
Raw HTTP error bodies and authentication headers are never logged.

`status` distinguishes pending, running, completed, failed and superseded work.
`reused` is a subset of completed work, not an additional mutually exclusive state.
An interrupted process leaves running work with expiring leases. `resume` waits
for active workers or reclaims expired work; it does not extract completed jobs
again. Explicit failures are terminal for that batch: use `retry` to create a new
attempt. Provider calls can repeat if a worker dies after the response but before
committing it; exactly-once billing is not guaranteed.

An active worker renews its lease while waiting for a model response. Transactions
fence commits using the job ID and a unique claim token. Expired or superseded
workers may leave an archived attempt, but cannot replace current results.

Sources are ordered by **acceptance into the database**. Each newly accepted
revision has a monotonically increasing job ID. A newer accepted revision
supersedes older pending/running work. Simultaneous submissions with identical
source hashes and settings share active work. Export timestamps do not determine
business facts or revision order; explicitly submitting old bytes later is a new
accepted revision.

## Inspect the queue while intake runs

```bash
python -m intake queue
python -m intake status --batch BATCH_ID
```

Or use the Python API from another process on the same host:

```python
from intake import Intake
app = Intake()
queue = app.queue()                 # consistent published snapshot
current = app.current()             # transactional database read
batches = app.store.batches()
progress = app.status(batches[0]["id"])
```

The notebook provides `run_intake(...)`, `retry_failed(...)`, `inspect_queue()`
and the same `app` API. Its parameters are `mode` (`intake`, `resume`, `retry`,
`refresh-policy`, `verify`), `documents`, `batch_id`, `force`, `mock`, `reports`,
`fail_on_error`, `saved_config`, `current_config`.
Reports default to false. The operator action prints the batch ID before work.
A saved-configuration resume also restores the configuration and responder used
by optional reports, including saved mock batches.

## State, history and coherent exports

SQLite is the source of truth. It transactionally stores batches, input bytes,
processing states, current records, immutable extraction attempts and claim tokens.
Input hashing and extraction use the **same captured bytes**. Each completed
extraction is committed independently; unrelated documents keep moving.
Databases created by steps 1–4 receive an additive schema upgrade on startup;
existing jobs and records are retained. Older rows do not gain invented settings.

Every completion commits to SQLite immediately. Filesystem snapshots are batched:
completion callbacks and a timer publish changed state at the configured interval,
then atomically replace `CURRENT.json` only after both files are durable. Actual
visibility delay includes publication time and database contention. A completed
batch always flushes the latest state; `export` forces an immediate publication.
While a batch is running, `app.current()` exposes committed state independently
of this filesystem cadence.

```text
deliverables/
  .state/intake.sqlite3
  CURRENT.json
  generations/<generation>/extractions.jsonl
  generations/<generation>/queue.json
  history/<document_id>/<attempt_id>.json
  routing-history/<document_id>/<routing_event_id>.json
  extractions.jsonl
  queue.json
```

`app.snapshot()` reads the manifest once and returns the matching immutable pair.
`app.queue()` uses that reader. Both files and the manifest carry a generation ID.
The manifest/queue also identify the database `state_revision` included in the
snapshot. Publication timing and acknowledged revisions are shared in SQLite so
overlapping operators do not export unchanged state independently. This is separate
from each document's accepted source revision. History is durable in SQLite at
commit; its filesystem copies are materialized before the corresponding snapshot
becomes visible.
The conventional root JSON files remain individually atomic compatibility exports
for submission; readers needing a matching pair must use the manifest/API.

If publication stops mid-write, the previous published generation stays readable.
Committed results remain in SQLite. `resume` or `python -m intake export` repairs
publication without model calls. After a crash following the manifest switch,
root compatibility files may lag until that repair. Old generations are retained
so readers remain safe; no automatic retention/cleanup policy is implemented.

A failed later attempt becomes the current error with a null extraction and a
`last_success` pointer into history. Other records and earlier hashes remain.
Per-record configuration and policy versions are authoritative: partial batches
can legitimately contain records produced by different settings.

`refresh-policy` updates all current routes in one transaction and records each
change in `routing-history/`, linking the previous and new policy versions. It
preserves extraction bytes, settings fingerprints and immutable extraction history.
Repeated refresh under unchanged rules is a no-op. Input reuse also records any
routing change. Completions use the active policy inside their commit transaction,
so a worker with an earlier cached policy text cannot revert it. Do not run mixed
routing code versions against one store: restart workers after a routing deployment.

## Migrate the existing committed outputs

The repository includes historical provider outputs. Before starting new intake,
optionally import those records into an **empty** database:

```bash
python -m intake migrate
python -m intake verify
```

On a fresh checkout, run these two commands to inspect and verify the committed
outputs: the state database and snapshot generations are intentionally not
committed. Migration rebuilds that local state without provider calls. Subsequent
`verify` checks also work under `python -O`; duplicates, altered queue facts or
retry commands, stale publication and unfinished work fail verification.

Migration checks source hashes and successful extractions, preserves response
provenance and old history paths, and archives imported current records in SQLite.
It refuses a nonempty database. Back up existing outputs before migration if you
want to retain their exact original formatting. Fingerprints now include provider
and endpoint identity, so historical records may require re-extraction on the next
intake. Starting intake without migration creates a fresh current state from that
batch; migrate first when existing records must be retained.

## Tests, accuracy and request evidence

```bash
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python -m intake verify

# Use a disposable mock output directory for reproducible examples.
python -m intake intake --mock --output /tmp/northstar-demo
python -m intake accuracy --mock --output /tmp/northstar-demo
python -m intake evidence --mock --output /tmp/northstar-demo

# Optional quality gate; still writes reports when comparisons/reviews fail.
python -m intake accuracy --mock --output /tmp/northstar-demo --fail-on-errors

# Optional provider observations: one extra extraction each, with configured retries.
python -m intake accuracy
python -m intake evidence
```

Offline tests use temporary directories. They cover all 20 fixture records,
policy examples, malformed output, refusal/truncation, source/settings changes,
unchanged reuse, failure after success, incremental visibility, heartbeat renewal,
actual worker termination/recovery, two independent worker processes, superseded
results and interrupted publication. They also cover unreadable files, Retry-After,
credential-redacted failed evidence, saved-setting retries/resume, additive database
upgrades, policy refresh and separate routing versus extraction deployments.
No live calls or credential setup are needed.

Evidence generation runs the same extraction/validation/retry pipeline as intake.
Failures still produce `request-evidence.json` with error/attempt details, HTTP
status when received and a nonzero CLI exit code. Invalid/missing sources and
malformed provider bodies are handled without an evidence-generation traceback.

Accuracy expectations now live separately in
`tests/fixtures/accuracy/expected.json`: 20 supplied messages plus the existing
paraphrase, each with source hashes/citations, null explanations, purpose facts,
required issues/evidence and independent expected routing. The loader checks the
references against source/policy/schema before any synthetic model work.

`accuracy.md` and `accuracy-results.json` report **12 literal scalar comparisons**
(240 supplied fields plus 12 synthetic), with no case or whitespace normalization.
The 11 non-purpose scalar metric is shown separately. Failed/missing/stale/invalid
records remain in the denominator and score zero. Stored routes and queue links
are checked against the reference without rerouting existing results.

Business-purpose wording and factual correctness are separate checks. Canonical
reference wording passes automatically; other nonempty wording needs a source-rubric
review, rather than receiving presence-only credit or being declared factually wrong.
Use `--purpose-reviews /path/to/reviews.json` for reviews bound to the expectation,
source and extraction hashes. Reviews cannot change strict exact-match counts or
rescue missing source evidence. `--expectations` selects an alternate reviewed
manifest. See `docs/accuracy.md` for counting rules, examples and the review format.

Earlier model outputs have already been viewed; the reference explicitly preserves
that disclosure and does not claim a blind evaluation. Replay fixture observations
do not establish model accuracy. Each configuration/source is reported separately.
Current `deliverables/accuracy.md` and `request-evidence.json` are offline mock
observations from the current implementation. The accuracy quality gate can fail
because the original replay fixtures contain incomplete evidence and purpose
wording awaiting review; reports retain those failures. Historical provider
observations remain under `deliverables/historical/2026-11-06/`. Operations
verification is documented in `docs/operations.md`.

## Workload verification

```bash
python -m intake benchmark --sizes 200 400 2000 \
  --report benchmarks/results.json --storage-dir .benchmark-work
```

The latest component audit passed all seven workload cases; its report is
`benchmarks/verification-2026-11-10.json`. It used the current engine with default
30-second leases and a 1-second publication interval. Earlier benchmark reports
remain historical observations with their original configurations.

The benchmark always uses generated mock messages and responses, isolated temporary
SQLite/output directories, real sleeps, fsync publication, snapshot readers and
spawned worker processes. It never uses provider credentials or modifies supplied
requests/review deliverables. Normal intake runs at every size; slow, throttled,
concurrent-operator and interrupted-worker scenarios run at the largest size.
Temporary workloads and event logs are cleaned up; measured results are retained.

`--workers`, `--latency-seconds`, `--poll-seconds`, `--timeout-seconds` and
`--publication-interval-seconds` make the profile explicit. Results include elapsed
time, throughput, publication/reader latency, transaction acquisition/hold timings,
storage growth, injected faults, duplicates and recovery assertions. See
`docs/benchmark.md` for the method, actual measurements and their limits. Mock
throughput measures the local persistence path, not provider speed or accuracy.

## Limits

The original 20-document live throughput measurement is historical. Current mock
benchmarks exercise up to 2,000 generated messages; they do not establish live
provider throughput, quota behavior or multi-day retention costs. Full snapshots
are retained, and publication still holds the database write lock during file I/O.
Tune the publication interval for your visibility/storage needs. No distributed
database adapter, shared automatic rate limiter or history cleanup
is included in steps 1–8.
Backups must include the database and any pre-migration history referenced by it.

The facilitator's capture setup records the coding session; commits capture Entire
checkpoints automatically. Commit/push and final submission remain separate actions.

committed extraction outputs. These are development fixtures, **not independently
authored accuracy expectations**. Records are labeled `response_source: mock`.
Mock and provider configurations have different fingerprints, preventing mock
results from being reused as live results. Unknown documents need new mock
fixtures or live extraction.

Multiple operator processes may use the same local state database and output
directory on that host. SQLite over NFS, Databricks Workspace/Volumes, or between
separate serverless/cluster hosts is unsupported. A multi-host deployment needs a
shared transactional database adapter; this version does not implement one.
Keep the database, source exports and history on persistent storage and back them
up. `/tmp` in these examples is for disposable demonstrations only.

## Browser dashboard (Flask)

Install the optional browser dependencies and start the app from the repository
root:

```bash
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements-web.lock
flask --app app run
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:5000**. The dashboard displays the existing review queue,
supports search and owner/status filters, and shows each request's extracted
facts, exact evidence quotes, review notes and next action. **Run mock intake**
starts work in the background; completed results update automatically. There are
no access-approval controls. Stop the local server with Ctrl+C. If running on a
remote development host, forward port 5000 to your computer before opening it.

The Flask entry point uses mock responses by default, with no API key needed.
It shares the CLI's durable state. On a fresh checkout, existing committed outputs
are imported without provider calls. An empty output directory starts with an
empty queue until intake is run. `INTAKE_SOURCE`, `INTAKE_OUTPUT`, `INTAKE_STATE`
and `INTAKE_WORKERS` configure its paths and workers. To deliberately use the
configured live provider instead, set `INTAKE_WEB_MODE=provider` along with the
provider environment variables below before starting Flask.

An equivalent command using the existing CLI is:

```bash
python -m intake serve --mock --port 5000
```

Flask and its transitive dependencies are pinned in `requirements-web.lock` and
declared as the optional `web` dependency group in `pyproject.toml`. The core CLI
remains usable without Flask. Run the full suite including browser route tests
inside the virtual environment:

```bash
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Without the web dependencies, browser tests are explicitly skipped. Browser tests
exercise Flask routes, mock intake/reuse, concurrent reads, duplicate start
protection, request validation, redacted errors and fresh-checkout import.

## Live provider configuration

The implemented provider is Databricks AI Gateway Chat Completions:
`POST <workspace-url>/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1/chat/completions`, with strict JSON schema
response formatting and default model `system.ai.gpt-6-luna`. The original
2026-11-06 outputs document observations of that configuration; the refactored
client has been tested offline, not against the live provider in this session.
Availability and permissions depend on your workspace.

For API-key authentication, supply these through your environment or secret
manager:

```bash
export INTAKE_AUTH=api_key
export INTAKE_BASE_URL=https://your-workspace-host
# Supply API_KEY through your environment; never commit it.
python -m intake intake
```

For notebook workspace authentication, use `INTAKE_AUTH=workspace`; the Databricks
SDK is imported lazily only when making a live call. This optional path depends
on the SDK already provided by your notebook runtime. It is not needed by offline
commands or API-key authentication. The notebook must run on the same supported
application host/storage arrangement as the CLI. The old assumption that separate
Databricks serverless resources could safely share filesystem state is superseded.

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `API_KEY` | unset | Live bearer credential; never stored in state or evidence |
| `INTAKE_AUTH` | `api_key` if API_KEY exists, otherwise `workspace` | Authentication strategy |
| `INTAKE_BASE_URL` | unset | Workspace origin; required with API-key auth, otherwise SDK host |
| `INTAKE_API_PATH` | `mlflow/v1/chat/completions` | Relative Chat Completions endpoint beneath `/ai-gateway/` |
| `INTAKE_MODEL` | `system.ai.gpt-6-luna` | Model service identifier |
| `INTAKE_MAX_TOKENS` | `4000` | Completion token limit |
| `INTAKE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `90` | HTTP timeout |
| `INTAKE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `4` | Retryable extraction attempts |
| `INTAKE_WORKERS` | `4` | Python API/notebook worker count; CLI `--workers` defaults to 4 |
| `INTAKE_LEASE_SECONDS` | `30` | Worker claim duration; heartbeat every third of this interval |
| `INTAKE_PUBLISH_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | `1` | Shared-state publication cadence; `0` requests publication after each completion |
| `INTAKE_STATE` | `<output>/.state/intake.sqlite3` | Local durable SQLite path; CLI `--state` overrides it |
